wins.text: Q2 revenue exceeded $2 billion for the first time in company history, with sales growth of 8.6% — the strongest daily sales rate since Q1 2023
EPS of $0.29 rose 12.7% year-over-year; operating margin reached 21%, up 80 bps YoY with incremental margins exactly at 30%

Contract signings hit 84 in Q2, well ahead of the prior 2 quarters; contract customer sales grew 11% and now represent 73.2% of revenue, up from 71.2% a year ago; national/regional/government contracts grew at a double-digit rate for 15 consecutive months
E-business surpassed 30% of sales for the first time ever in Q2, growing 13.5% YoY; combined digital footprint (FMI + e-business) reached 61% of sales, up from mid-50s two years ago
Non-manufacturing sites in the $50,000+ category saw revenue increase 30% YoY with site count up over 18%; all customer site categories $5,000+ showed double-digit site count growth in June

risks.text: End market demand remains sluggish with PMI sub-50 for most of the past ~2.5 years; management explicitly noted 'limited visibility' and shared customers' uncertainty over trade policy impact on 2025 demand

Tariff environment is volatile and unpredictable — pricing actions came in at 140-170 bps in Q2 vs. the 3%-4% exit-rate target communicated on the Q1 call, reflecting timing slippage due to tariff pauses and policy changes
Gross margin faces price/cost headwinds in H2 2025 as higher-cost tariffed inventory flows through COGS; management acknowledged price/cost 'gets more challenging as we get deeper into it'
Inventory up 14.7% YoY and expected to remain elevated through 2025 as the company navigates tariffs and builds in inflation, pressuring working capital and cash conversion

FMI device signings softened — tariff-related customer conversations consumed bandwidth, reducing FMI expansion discussions; full-year MEU signings now guided to 25,000-26,000, slightly below prior ambitions

guidance_items.detail: Management expressed confidence in achieving double-digit sales growth in H2 2025, supported by strong contract pipeline and accelerating pricing; no prior explicit H2 revenue guide to compare against, but tone is meaningfully more bullish than prior cautious stance
Gross margin for full-year 2025 expected to remain essentially flat with 2024; price/cost acknowledged as a growing headwind in H2
Full-year capex guided to $250M-$270M, unchanged from prior guidance, up from $214M in 2024
Pricing impact expected to reach 3%-5% in Q3 and potentially 5%-8% by year-end, up from 140-170 bps realized in Q2, contingent on tariff developments
FMI MEU signings for full year guided to 25,000-26,000 equivalent weighted devices

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Competitive response to Fastenal's accelerating market share gains — how are rivals defending share?
Contribution margin profile and profitability evolution of $10,000+/month customer sites over time
Pricing shortfall vs. Q1 guidance (140-170 bps realized vs. 3%-4% exit-rate target communicated last quarter)
